target.title: fix(codex): guard sandbox http/request JSON.parse against non-JSON stdout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`runSandboxHttpRequest` in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/http.ts` parsed the sandbox shell helper's stdout with an unguarded `JSON.parse` (line 91). When the helper exits 0 but emits non-JSON (startup banner, debug log interleaved with the response, stdout truncated by `maxBuffer`, or SIGPIPE), the raw `SyntaxError` bubbled up to the JSON-RPC dispatcher as an opaque error (`Unexpected token ...`) with no mention of `sandbox http/request`, making root-cause hard to identify.

## Why This Change Was Made

Same `JSON.parse` guard pattern shipped this week across matrix (#97973), sms (#97999), signal (#98073), plugin-sdk (#98125), telegram ingress (#98372), and qmd mcporter (#98381). The streaming sibling in this same file (`runStreamingSandboxHttpRequest`) already wraps each stdout line via `requireObject(JSON.parse(line))`; the non-streaming path was missed.

The thrown message is kept generic on purpose. `JSON.parse`'s `SyntaxError` embeds a snippet of the raw input, which is surfaced before session visibility filtering; placing that snippet on the thrown Error (or on `.cause`, which `formatErrorMessage` walks into the user-visible path) would leak raw sandbox stdout. The guard throws a typed, attributable error with a generic message instead.

## User Impact

A Codex `http/request` tool whose sandbox helper emits non-JSON stdout now fails with a clear `sandbox http/request returned non-JSON stdout` error instead of an opaque `Unexpected token ...` SyntaxError. Valid JSON responses and the happy path are unchanged.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** A non-JSON sandbox helper stdout (exit 0) threw a raw `SyntaxError` out of `runSandboxHttpRequest`, surfaced by the JSON-RPC dispatcher as an opaque error with no sandbox context.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node v24.14.0, commit `935aa82dab` on branch `fix/codex-sandbox-http-jsonparse-guard`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node --import tsx verify-codex-sandbox-http-real.mjs` — drives the real exported `httpRequest` JSON-RPC handler over a real exec-server WebSocket (replicating `sandbox-exec-server.test-helpers.ts` without the vitest `vi` dependency). Only the sandbox shell backend is mocked (there is no real sandbox helper in CI); `httpRequest -> runSandboxHttpRequest -> JSON.parse` runs for real. The backend returns `{code: 0, stdout: "<html>daemon warning</html>"}` and the script issues `initialize` then `http/request`.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (live stdout, copied verbatim — real exec-server, real WebSocket JSON-RPC):

  ```text
  $ node --import tsx verify-codex-sandbox-http-real.mjs
  drives the real httpRequest JSON-RPC path over a real exec-server WebSocket;
  only the sandbox shell backend is mocked (no real sandbox helper exists in CI).

  [agent/embedded] codex sandbox exec-server started

  backend returned: code=0, stdout='<html>daemon warning</html>' (non-JSON)
  http/request rejected -> error.message = "sandbox http/request returned non-JSON stdout"

  Verdict: real httpRequest path surfaces a typed 'non-JSON stdout' error (bug fixed)
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** The real `httpRequest` JSON-RPC path rejects with `sandbox http/request returned non-JSON stdout` when the sandbox helper returns a non-JSON stdout at exit 0, instead of an opaque SyntaxError. The error is attributable (`sandbox http/request`) and carries no raw stdout snippet.
- **What was not tested:** A real sandboxed shell helper emitting a daemon banner over a live network call (the sandbox helper has an SSRF guard that blocks loopback/private IPs, so a local HTTP server is not a faithful stand-in; the real exec-server + mocked shell backend is the closest non-mocked reproduction of the `httpRequest -> runSandboxHttpRequest` decision boundary). Valid-JSON regression is covered by `sandbox-exec-server.http.test.ts` (8 tests, incl. `routes HTTP requests through the sandbox backend`).

## Tests and validation

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server.http.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  8 passed (8)
```

Added `surfaces a typed error when the sandbox helper returns non-JSON stdout`: drives the real `httpRequest` JSON-RPC path with a mocked sandbox backend that returns a 0-exit non-JSON stdout, and asserts the rejection matches `/non-JSON stdout/i`.

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior: Yes (intended, bounded) - a non-JSON sandbox helper stdout now surfaces a typed, attributable error instead of an opaque SyntaxError; valid JSON and the happy path unchanged.
- Config/env/migration behavior: No - no config or env surface touched.
- Security/auth/secrets/network/tool execution: Yes (improvement) - the thrown message is generic and does not embed raw sandbox stdout or the SyntaxError raw-input snippet; no new credential, network, or command-execution path.
- Plugins/providers/channels/SDK: No - internal to the Codex sandbox exec-server; `runSandboxHttpRequest` keeps its return type.
- Highest-risk area: a future sandbox helper change that legitimately prints non-JSON to stdout on success - but that is exactly the case the guard makes attributable instead of opaque.
- Mitigation: 8 http tests (incl. the new non-JSON-stdout case) + node runtime verification driving the real `httpRequest` JSON-RPC path over a real exec-server WebSocket.

Closes: N/A (no existing issue)
